chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Murazam ibn Hakeem, from Abdul-A'ala, the freedman of the family of Saam, who said:

Indeed, the condition of Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) became severe until the people of Al-Madina were discussing it. So that reached him, and he designated a thousand Dirhams, then sent them to the governor of Al-Madina and said: 'This is the charity of my wealth.'

key_terms.اشْتَدَّتْ حَالُهُ: His condition/state became severe or difficult

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali ibn Al-Husayn respond to his period of hardship in Medina?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the generosity of Imam Ali ibn Al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) during a time of personal hardship, illustrating the Shia virtue of maintaining charitable giving even when resources are strained. By designating his wealth as *Sadaqah* and sending it to the governor of Medina, he demonstrated spiritual resilience and the importance of purifying one's assets through charity, a theme central to the chapter on the manifestation of divine bounty.

en.hubeali: From him, from Ali Bin Jadeed, from Murazam Bin Hakeym, from Abdul A’ala, a slave of the progeny of Saam who said,

‘The state of Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> was extremely difficult until the people of Al-Medina were discussing it. So that reached him<sup>asws</sup>, and he<sup>asws</sup> designated a thousand Dirhams, then sent with these to the governor of Al-Medina and said: ‘This is a charity from my<sup>asws</sup> wealth’.
en.sarwar: 13. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from Ali ibn Hadid from Murazim ibn Hakim from ‘ Abd al-‘A’la’ Mawla’Ale Sam who has said the following:

“Ali ibn al-Husayn, ‘Alayhim al-Salam, lived in serious financial condition and people of al-Madinah began to speak about it. It came to his notice. He assigned one thousand dirham and sent it to the governor of al-Madinah saying, ‘It is the charity due on our assets.’”
